summary: Shows setting the keyring and required signature count through environment variables, ignoring specific GnuPG status codes such as NO_PUBKEY with `--ignore-signature-status-code`, and that failed verification blocks the install. Verification can be disabled with `--disable-gpg-verify` or GALAXY_DISABLE_GPG_VERIFY.
questions: How do I set the galaxy keyring and signature count with environment variables?
How can I ignore NO_PUBKEY errors during collection signature verification?
What happens if a collection's signature check fails?
How do I turn off GPG verification for ansible-galaxy?

answer_card.title: Ignore GnuPG errors or disable verification
answer_card.answer_md:
You can configure verification through environment variables:

```bash
export ANSIBLE_GALAXY_GPG_KEYRING=~/.ansible/pubring.kbx
export ANSIBLE_GALAXY_REQUIRED_VALID_SIGNATURE_COUNT=all
ansible-galaxy collection install my_namespace.my_collection --ignore-signature-status-code NO_PUBKEY
```

`--ignore-signature-status-code` can be repeated to ignore several GnuPG status codes; then only other errors are shown.

If verification fails, the collection is **not** installed. To disable GnuPG verification entirely, use `--disable-gpg-verify` or set `GALAXY_DISABLE_GPG_VERIFY`.
